extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, applicants, institutional administrators, and NIH staff involved in grants and peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A news-index page summarizing recent NIH updates, reminders, and resources that inform how investigators should prepare and submit grant applications and how applications are reviewed and scored. The page highlights policy changes, new templates, and initiatives affecting NIH extramural funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of research models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance emphasizes choosing the model(s) that best address the scientific question; NIH supports NAMs but expects scientific appropriateness and human relevance be justified in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should learn the PF5 key features and required application format; be aware that applications can be administratively split into linked awards after peer review (before Just-in-Time), so plan consortium/linked award structure accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for pilot use the new simplified 2026 format and include the specified required elements; this is a resource to align applicant DMS plans with NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for embedding replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should address replication and reproducibility where relevant in applications and proposals; NIH will emphasize and incentivize replication/reproducibility through initiatives and highlighted topics — consider study design, power, methods, and plans that enable replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and handling of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' score designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains an NIH review-process modification: applications in the middle third are labeled 'competitive but not discussed.' Applicants should understand this designation and its implications for discussion and scoring in the context of review-process changes implemented after the lapse in appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) — expected effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in peer review. Applicants and institutional staff should be aware of process changes resulting from CSR consolidation and consult NIH updates for operational details and any implications for submissions and review timelines.
